title: Counting model with rat-data checks: at label doses, contrast-based functional ultrasound in 2–5 mm adult cortical voxels is bubble-limited; contrast-free Doppler wins above about −20 dB SNR
abstract: At the doses that product labels allow, too few microbubbles flow through a 2-5 mm piece of adult cortex for contrast agents to make transcranial functional ultrasound fast; contrast-free Doppler is the faster mode whenever its per-frame blood signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is above about -20 dB. This matters because groups that want wearable, noninvasive functional ultrasound for adults must choose between contrast-free power Doppler (echo power of moving blood), contrast-enhanced power Doppler and functional ultrasound localization microscopy (fULM, which counts tracked single bubbles). We wrote a variance model with speckle, thermal noise, bubble shot noise (random number and brightness of bubbles in a voxel), track-count statistics, localization density and a label-dose budget, and tested its parts on public rat data (3D ULM tracks; 2D contrast IQ data, 107 blocks at 15 MHz). In the rat data, contrast Doppler noise was 17-1000 times larger than speckle predicts, track counts were close to Poisson after regional detrending (dispersion 1.02-1.24), and contrast power had 0.6-2 times the variance of track counts in the same voxels, rising with window length. With human literature values (2 MHz, 4.5 cm deep, expected z = 3, Monte Carlo median and 10-90 %): the largest 3 % of SonoVue-like bubbles give 80 % of the echo; localization density caps fULM at about 0.01 tracks per s per mm3, about 600 times fewer than in rat fULM; a 20 % flow change needs 160 min per condition (40-650) in a 2-mm voxel and 15 min in a 5-mm voxel. At the label maximum, one session can detect at best a 28 % change in a 2-mm voxel with fULM for SonoVue, 36 % for Definity and 14 % for Optison. Contrast-free Doppler is faster than both contrast modes above -18.8 dB (-21.1 to -16.8 dB) per frame for a 3-mm voxel, -22.0 dB with a band-limited estimator; over localization densities of 0.01-1 bubble per cell the threshold stays between -24 and -16 dB. Main limitation: the per-frame cortical blood SNR through the temporal window has not been measured, and published data cannot place it on either side of the threshold; we give a protocol to measure it.

(b) Contrast-free SNR above which contrast-free Doppler is faster, against localization density, for a 3-mm voxel. Bands: 10-90 % Monte Carlo ranges.
